title: Aphrody OS: Bun runtime and native SDK architecture
summary: The Bun fork, shared native C ABI and TypeScript SDK behind Aphrody OS, with separate source and deployment contracts.
content:
# Aphrody OS runtime and native SDK

Aphrody OS brings a browser interface, a desktop shell and a cross-platform CLI around shared capability owners. The runtime is the unmodified upstream Bun canary. Product workflows and the canonical interface remain in the Aphrody monorepo.

## Bun runtime

Bun provides the JavaScriptCore runtime, Web APIs, bundler, package manager and test runner. Fork API documentation lives in the fork's `docs/` tree. Aphrody records its selected documentation revision in `docs/reference/upstream-bun/SOURCE.json`; it does not maintain a second Bun documentation tree.

## Native SDK

`packages/engine/runtime` declares `@aphrody/runtime-sdk`. Its FFI loader uses `dlopen` from `bun:ffi`. The native library boundary is `aphrody_ffi` in `crates/interop/ffi`, and `include/aphrody.h` retains the `aphrody_*` and `yolo_*` compatibility identities. The ABI contract requires version checks, opaque handles and library-owned buffer release.

## Qualification

Source declarations do not prove that every native module is installed or active on every platform. Check the selected artifact, ABI and target before enabling a native capability.

## Source references

- [Aphrody architecture and active plan](https://github.com/aphrody-labs/aphrody/blob/main/PLAN.md)
- [Native ABI header](https://github.com/aphrody-labs/aphrody/blob/main/crates/interop/ffi/include/aphrody.h)
- [Runtime SDK](https://github.com/aphrody-labs/aphrody/tree/main/packages/engine/runtime)

title: Bun, Next.js and Material in the Aphrody UI
summary: Where the runtime, shared M3 framework and product UI are owned, and how web and desktop frontends consume them.
content:
# Bun, Material and the Aphrody UI

Upstream Bun owns the runtime, built-in modules and build tooling. Material owns the shared Material 3 framework, tokens, libm3, controls and canonical @aphrody/app-ui source. Aphrody owns product workflows and integrates those shared interfaces.

## Shared interface

Material's pinned app-ui source provides the shared UI package consumed by Aphrody's web and desktop products. Aphrody retains product routes, host integration and application behavior. A source pin or successful frontend build does not by itself prove native rendering or deployment.

## Framework adapters

Material owns its Material 3 and Next.js packages; Tailwind retains its own source and build contract. Consult each selected package manifest and its owner documentation before choosing an API. Package presence does not prove production activation or comparative performance.

## Source references

title: Material 3 color tokens and dynamic themes
summary: Material 3 dynamic schemes and native tokens, with the remaining web-to-native convergence stated explicitly.
content:
# Material 3 color tokens

The Material 3 source provides the TypeScript dynamic-color API in packages/m3-tokens/src/dynamic-color.ts. The native token engine is owned by crates/m3-tokens; crates/libm3 consumes that engine and crates/libm3-wasm exposes its scalar ABI.

## Web and native boundary

The web dynamic-color API and native Rust token engine currently remain separate implementations inside the Material ownership workspace. Material's active plan still tracks routing the web API through the qualified native binding; repository ownership alone does not prove that convergence.

## HCT and semantic roles

HCT represents hue, chroma and tone. A seed and scheme configuration resolve semantic roles such as primary and surface with associated foreground colors. Components consume roles rather than assuming one hexadecimal value fits every theme.

## Contrast and accessibility

Theme configuration is not a blanket accessibility guarantee. Check contrast, keyboard navigation, focus indicators and readable text in rendered light and dark interfaces, including custom component states.

## Source references

- [TypeScript dynamic-color API](https://github.com/aphrody-labs/aphrody-m3/blob/main/packages/m3-tokens/src/dynamic-color.ts)

title: Aphrody desktop: CEF, Tauri and the shared UI bridge
summary: The canonical desktop shell, its frontend configuration and the RPC shared with the web application.
content:
# Aphrody desktop and the shared UI

The desktop shell lives in Aphrody's crates/ui/app. Its manifest selects tauri-runtime-cef; its Tauri configuration sets frontendDist to ui-dist and declares the main window. Material pins the shared frontend source from aphrody-app-ui, while Aphrody owns the product shell and host integration.

## Shared RPC

The shared frontend bridge routes aphrodyRpc through the aphrody_rpc desktop command inside Tauri and through same-origin POST /rpc in the browser. The app-server requires an initialization handshake. Studio also contains explicitly registered native commands; a web route does not automatically gain desktop privileges.

## Deployment boundary

A configured frontend and a compiled shell are separate from an installed application running on a physical desktop. Check the installed artifact and its supported target before claiming native activation. The former apps/web ping bridge is not the current architecture.

- [Aphrody desktop shell](https://github.com/aphrody-labs/aphrody/tree/main/crates/ui/app)

title: Aphrody agent context, llms.txt and isolated memory
summary: Repository guidance, public AI-readable context and domain-isolated memory, without implicit provider synchronization.
content:
# Agent context and isolated memory

`AGENTS.md` defines repository conventions and capability ownership. `PLAN.md` records the active architecture and queue, while `MEMORY.md` records dated evidence and limits. These files guide coding agents; they do not change model training.

## Public context

The live `https://aphrody.com/llms.txt` endpoint returned an Aphrody overview during the 2026-10-09 audit. Treat it as a public context document rather than a guarantee of search indexing, ranking or deployment completeness.

## Native memory

`aphrody home` and `aphrody graph` provide the native home and graph surfaces. The `aphrody` and `ie` profiles remain isolated. Provider authentication, cookies and raw provider histories stay in their protected stores; no provider-memory synchronization is implied.

## Source references

- [Public llms.txt](https://aphrody.com/llms.txt)
